claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced or severe lattice distortion relative to commercially pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr creates heterogeneous local stress fields.
The lattice-distortion-induced stress field facilitates dislocation cross-slip at 600–900°C.
Lattice distortion facilitates dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr during high-temperature deformation.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery reduce dislocation pile-up in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced cross-slip produces a more homogeneous dislocation distribution.
More numerous pathways for dislocation motion can contribute to greater ductility.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and a more homogeneous dislocation distribution delay local stress concentration and crack initiation.
WTaTiVZr consequently has greater plastic strain or ductility than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
WTaTiVZr consequently has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Nearly equivalent atomic sizes in WTaTiVZr produce strong lattice distortion.
Pure tungsten lacks the proposed distortion-driven cross-slip and recovery mechanisms.
Commercially pure tungsten typically exhibits significant dislocation pile-up and lower plastic strain and toughness under high-temperature mechanical loading.
After equivalent deformation, WTaTiVZr will have less dislocation-density buildup near crack-initiation sites than pure tungsten.
Post-mortem TEM will show more evidence of cross-slip and dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism is expected to be dominant between 600°C and 900°C.
Different deformation mechanisms may govern at lower temperatures or under different loading regimes.
Thermally activated recovery or recrystallization processes may overlap with the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator invokes severe lattice distortion, while the mechanism attributes that distortion to nearly equivalent atomic sizes. Without another source of distortion, near-equivalent sizes do not coherently explain severe size-mismatch-induced lattice distortion.
